sections.overview: Isturgia limbaria, the Frosted Yellow, is a day-flying geometrid moth of western and central Europe, extending into parts of southern Europe.
sections.identification: Its yellow to orange-yellow wings have a contrasting chocolate-brown border, more pronounced in males; male antennae are feathered.
sections.habitat: It inhabits broom-rich heathland, often on sandy soils, as well as sunny woodland edges and clearings where broom grows.
sections.diet: Its caterpillars feed on broom shrubs, especially Cytisus scoparius.
sections.behavior: Adults fly by day from spring into summer, with one or two generations depending on region and conditions.
sections.reproduction: The species overwinters as a pupa; caterpillars develop through the warmer months.
sections.ecology: Its distribution and breeding sites track broom-rich heath and scrub; no close-cousin comparison is established in the sources reviewed.
sections.conservation: Loss of sandy grassland and heath through land conversion is identified as a regional pressure in central Europe.
